anchor.text: Though they became independent entities upon their liberation from Spain, both Peru and Bolivia maintained popular movements for reunification. In 1827, Peruvian forces invaded Bolivia with the intent to create a shared government, entering L2Paz in 1828 and forcing the resignation of Antonio José de Sucre, a close ally of Simén Bolivar, who maintained his own msion of South American unity under his nation of Gran Colombia. Subsequent years were chaotic, including the declaration of war by Gran Colombia on Peru, which came to an end with the deaths of both Sucre and Bolivar in 1830. A unification plan was not put in place until 1836, with the emergence of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation, composed of three states: Baliviz, North Peru, and South Peru; the confederation was motivated by both a shared history and ethnic similarities, but also byplans for a reemergence of the commercial prominence that the region had previously enjoyed when united under Spanish whonty, However, the state was loosely arranged and short-lived. Argentina and Chile, fearful of the influence that a unified Sate of such magnitude could wield, quickly entered into an alliance to confront and dissolve the combined state in the War of the Confederation, which concluded with the Battle of Yungay in 1839, after which both Peru and Bolivia were restored as ent nations, _ During the Confederation, the coinage of the state was altered appropriately.
